records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה רְאֵ֛ה נְתַתִּ֥יךָ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְפַרְעֹ֑ה וְאַהֲרֹ֥ן אָחִ֖יךָ יִהְיֶ֥ה נְבִיאֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, see, I have made you God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "See, I have appointed you to be as God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will serve as your prophet.

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "See, I have made you God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother will be your prophet.

R.1: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Listen. I am making you like God to Pharaoh. Your brother Aaron will speak for you, the way a prophet speaks for God.

decisions.choice: I have made you God to Pharaoh: Moses will stand before Pharaoh with God's authority
decisions.reason: The word for God has no article and can also mean "a god". Moses is not made divine; he is to Pharaoh what God is to a prophet, the one whose word is passed on. God said the same about Moses and Aaron in 4:16. The verb is in the past tense of something already settled.

decisions.choice: your prophet: the one who speaks for you
decisions.reason: A prophet speaks the words another gives him. In 4:16 Aaron is called Moses' "mouth"; here the same relationship is called being his prophet.

decisions.choice: the way a prophet speaks for God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what being Moses' prophet means, as 4:16 and verse 2 show.

records.heading: Moses and Aaron before Pharaoh

records.source: אַתָּ֣ה תְדַבֵּ֔ר אֵ֖ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲצַוֶּ֑ךָּ וְאַהֲרֹ֤ן אָחִ֨יךָ֙ יְדַבֵּ֣ר אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְשִׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאַרְצֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: You, you will speak all that I command you, and Aaron your brother will speak to Pharaoh, and he will let go [the] sons of Israel from his land.
pieces: Say everything I give you to say. Then your brother Aaron will speak to Pharaoh, so that he lets the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} leave his land.

L.2: You shall speak all that I command you, and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he let the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel go from his land.

R.2: Tell Aaron everything I command you. Then your brother Aaron will tell Pharaoh to let the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} leave his country.

decisions.choice: you, you will speak: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: God's word goes first to Moses, then through Aaron to Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: and he will let go: the aim of the message
alternatives: and he will let go (a prediction)
decisions.reason: The clause states what Aaron's speaking is meant to bring about: that Pharaoh release Israel.

decisions.choice: Tell Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom Moses speaks; verse 1 and 4:15-16 show that Moses gives the words to Aaron.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֥י אַקְשֶׁ֖ה אֶת־לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֧י אֶת־אֹתֹתַ֛י וְאֶת־מוֹפְתַ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And I, I will make hard the heart of Pharaoh, and I will multiply my signs and my wonders in [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: As for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will make Pharaoh's heart hard, and I will fill the land of Egypt with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} signs and wonders.

L.3: But I will make the heart of Pharaoh hard, and I will multiply {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} signs and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wonders in the land of Egypt.

R.3: But I will make Pharaoh stubborn. I will do many miracles and wonders in Egypt.

decisions.choice: I will make hard: one of three verbs for Pharaoh's heart
decisions.reason: Exodus uses three verbs for what happens to Pharaoh's heart: "make hard" (here and 13:15), "be strong" or "make strong" (4:21; 7:13, 22; 9:12), and "be heavy" or "make heavy" (7:14; 8:11, 28; the same root is used of the heavy labor in 5:9). All three describe a will set firmly against God's command; the heart is the seat of thought and will. Sometimes God is the subject (4:21; 7:3), sometimes Pharaoh himself (8:11, 28), and sometimes the heart simply "is" hard or heavy (7:13, 14, 22). The text holds these together without explaining how.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: acts that show God's power and point to him
decisions.reason: A "sign" points to something beyond itself (4:8-9); a "wonder" is an extraordinary act. The pair is used later of the whole Exodus (Deuteronomy 4:34; 6:22; Psalm 135:9).

decisions.choice: make Pharaoh's heart hard (Balanced); make Pharaoh stubborn (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "hard" for this verb, "strong" (Literal) for the verb in 4:21 and 7:13, and "heavy" (Literal) for 7:14. Readable says plainly what a hard heart is.

decisions.choice: fill the land of Egypt with
decisions.reason: "Multiply" means to do many; Balanced says it as filling the land with them.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־יִשְׁמַ֤ע אֲלֵכֶם֙ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְנָתַתִּ֥י אֶת־יָדִ֖י בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְהוֹצֵאתִ֨י אֶת־צִבְאֹתַ֜י אֶת־עַמִּ֤י בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בִּשְׁפָטִ֖ים גְּדֹלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And not will listen to you Pharaoh, and I will put my hand on Egypt and I will bring out my hosts, my people, [the] sons of Israel, from [the] land of Egypt with great judgments.
pieces: Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against Egypt and, with great judgments, lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} ranks, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, out of the land of Egypt.

L.4: And Pharaoh will not listen to you, and I will put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand on Egypt and bring out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hosts, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, from the land of Egypt with great judgments.

R.4: Pharaoh will not listen to you. Then I will use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against Egypt. I will punish Egypt severely, and I will lead {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, out of Egypt like an army marching out.

decisions.choice: put my hand on Egypt: act against Egypt with power
decisions.reason: God's "hand" is his power at work (3:19-20; 6:1).

decisions.choice: my hosts: Israel as an organized company, like an army
decisions.reason: The word means armies or ordered ranks. Israel leaves Egypt in ordered groups (6:26; 12:41, 51), as God's own company.

decisions.choice: great judgments: punishments God carries out as judge
decisions.reason: The word is used of God's acts against Egypt in 6:6 and 12:12, where they fall on "all the gods of Egypt".

decisions.choice: punish Egypt severely ... like an army marching out
decisions.reason: Readable says what "great judgments" and "hosts" mean here.

records.source: וְיָדְע֤וּ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בִּנְטֹתִ֥י אֶת־יָדִ֖י עַל־מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהוֹצֵאתִ֥י אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִתּוֹכָֽם׃
records.gloss: And will know Egypt that I [am] Yahweh, when I stretch out my hand over Egypt and I bring out [the] sons of Israel from among them.
pieces: When I reach out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand against Egypt and lead the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out from among its people, the Egyptians will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.5: And the Egyptians will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when I stretch out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand over Egypt and bring out the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel from among them."

R.5: Then the Egyptians will learn that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will learn it when I use {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} power against them and take the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} out of their land."

decisions.choice: they will know that I am Yahweh: the answer to Pharaoh's words in 5:2
decisions.reason: Pharaoh said, "I do not know Yahweh" (5:2). The plagues and the Exodus are to make him and Egypt know (7:17; 8:18; 14:4, 18), as Israel too will know (6:7).

decisions.choice: Egypt: the people of Egypt
decisions.reason: The name of the land stands for its people, as the plural verb shows.

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְאַהֲרֹ֑ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֹתָ֖ם כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ׃
records.gloss: And did Moses and Aaron just as commanded Yahweh them, so they did.
pieces: So Moses and Aaron obeyed; they did just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them.

L.6: And Moses and Aaron did [so]; just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded them, so they did.

R.6: Moses and Aaron obeyed. They did everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told them to do.

decisions.choice: so they did: the repetition stresses full obedience
decisions.reason: The verse says twice that they did it, a way of saying they did exactly as commanded (compare Genesis 6:22).

records.source: וּמֹשֶׁה֙ בֶּן־שְׁמֹנִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְאַֽהֲרֹ֔ן בֶּן־שָׁלֹ֥שׁ וּשְׁמֹנִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה בְּדַבְּרָ֖ם אֶל־פַּרְעֹֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And Moses [was a] son of eighty years, and Aaron [a] son of three and eighty years, when they spoke to Pharaoh.
pieces: At the time they spoke to Pharaoh, Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron was eighty-three.

L.7: And Moses [was] a son of eighty years, and Aaron a son of eighty-three years, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

R.7: When Moses and Aaron spoke to Pharaoh, Moses was eighty years old. Aaron was eighty-three.

decisions.choice: a son of eighty years: eighty years old
decisions.reason: "Son of" a number of years is the usual way of giving a person's age.

decisions.choice: eighty and eighty-three: Aaron is the older brother
decisions.reason: Aaron is three years older than Moses. Moses dies at the age of 120 (Deuteronomy 34:7).

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses and Aaron,

records.heading: Aaron's staff becomes a serpent

records.source: כִּי֩ יְדַבֵּ֨ר אֲלֵכֶ֤ם פַּרְעֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנ֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם מוֹפֵ֑ת וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַ֧ח אֶֽת־מַטְּךָ֛ וְהַשְׁלֵ֥ךְ לִפְנֵֽי־פַרְעֹ֖ה יְהִ֥י לְתַנִּֽין׃
records.gloss: When speaks to you Pharaoh, saying, give for yourselves [a] wonder, and you shall say to Aaron, take your staff and throw [it] before Pharaoh; it will become [a] serpent.
pieces: "If Pharaoh demands, 'Prove yourselves with a wonder,' tell Aaron to take his staff and throw it down in front of Pharaoh. It will turn into a serpent."

L.9: "When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, 'Give a wonder for yourselves,' then you shall say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and throw [it] down before Pharaoh'; it will become a serpent."

R.9: "Pharaoh will say to you, 'Show me a miracle.' Then, Moses, tell Aaron to throw his staff down in front of Pharaoh. It will turn into a serpent."

decisions.choice: give for yourselves a wonder: perform a wonder to prove your claim
alternatives: give a wonder (as a sign) for you
decisions.reason: Pharaoh will ask for a sign that shows Moses and Aaron are sent by a god. "For yourselves" means on your own behalf, as your proof.

decisions.choice: serpent: a large reptile, a different word from the "snake" of 4:3
decisions.reason: The word is used of great sea creatures (Genesis 1:21), of dangerous serpents (Deuteronomy 32:33; Psalm 91:13), and of Pharaoh pictured as a great monster lying in his rivers (Ezekiel 29:3). Here it may be a large snake or a crocodile. Verse 15 calls the staff that turned into a "snake" (4:3) by the other word, so the two words overlap.

decisions.choice: Moses
decisions.reason: "You shall say" is singular: Moses is to tell Aaron. Readable names him.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיַּ֣עַשׂוּכֵ֔ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת־מַטֵּ֗הוּ לִפְנֵ֥י פַרְעֹ֛ה וְלִפְנֵ֥י עֲבָדָ֖יו וַיְהִ֥י לְתַנִּֽין׃
records.gloss: And went Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and they did so, just as had commanded Yahweh, and threw Aaron his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became [a] serpent.
pieces: Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded. Aaron cast his staff to the ground before Pharaoh and his court, and it turned into a serpent.

L.10: And Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did so, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded; and Aaron threw down his staff before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

R.10: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh. They did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them. Aaron threw his staff down in front of Pharaoh and his officials. The staff became a serpent.

decisions.choice: his servants: Pharaoh's officials
decisions.reason: The king's "servants" are the members of his court (5:21).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָא֙ גַּם־פַּרְעֹ֔ה לַֽחֲכָמִ֖ים וְלַֽמְכַשְּׁפִ֑ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֨וּ גַם־הֵ֜ם חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֛יִם בְּלַהֲטֵיהֶ֖ם כֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And summoned also Pharaoh the wise men and the sorcerers, and did also they, [the] magicians of Egypt, by their enchantments thus.
pieces: Pharaoh in turn called for his wise men and sorcerers, and the magicians of Egypt did the same thing with their spells.

L.11: And Pharaoh also summoned the wise men and the sorcerers; and they also, the magicians of Egypt, did thus by their enchantments.

R.11: Then Pharaoh called for his wise men and his sorcerers. These Egyptian magicians used their magic and did the same thing.

decisions.choice: magicians: experts in sacred writings and secret knowledge
decisions.reason: The word is used only of experts at foreign courts: those who could not interpret Pharaoh's dreams (Genesis 41:8, 24) and the wise men of Babylon (Daniel 1:20; 2:2). It seems to name the same people as the "wise men" and "sorcerers" just mentioned.

decisions.choice: their enchantments: their secret arts, their spells
decisions.reason: The word is related to words for what is hidden or done secretly. The text does not say how the magicians did it; it shows that they could imitate the sign but not overcome it (verse 12).

decisions.choice: sorcerers: those who practice magic
decisions.reason: The same word is used of practices forbidden in Israel (22:17; Deuteronomy 18:10).

records.source: וַיַּשְׁלִ֨יכוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מַטֵּ֔הוּ וַיִּהְי֖וּ לְתַנִּינִ֑ם וַיִּבְלַ֥ע מַטֵּֽה־אַהֲרֹ֖ן אֶת־מַטֹּתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And threw down each man his staff, and they became serpents; and swallowed [the] staff of Aaron their staffs.
pieces: Every one of them threw his staff to the ground, and these too became serpents. Then Aaron's staff swallowed theirs.

L.12: And they threw down each man his staff, and they became serpents; but the staff of Aaron swallowed up their staffs.

R.12: Each man threw down his staff, and each one turned into a serpent. But then Aaron's staff swallowed every one of their staffs.

decisions.choice: swallowed: Aaron's staff overcame theirs
decisions.reason: The staff had become a serpent, yet the text says "Aaron's staff" swallowed them: God's sign defeats Egypt's magic. The same verb is used when the earth swallows the Egyptians at the sea (15:12).

records.source: וַיֶּחֱזַק֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And was strong [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he listened to them, just as had spoken Yahweh.
pieces: But Pharaoh's heart remained stubborn. He refused to listen to them, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said he would.

L.13: And the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not listen to them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken.

R.13: But Pharaoh stayed stubborn. He would not listen to Moses and Aaron. This is just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen.

decisions.choice: was strong: Pharaoh's heart stayed firm against God
decisions.reason: This is the verb of 4:21, "make strong"; here the heart itself is the subject. See the note on 7:3 for the three verbs used for Pharaoh's heart.

decisions.choice: just as Yahweh had spoken: as God said in verses 3-4 and 4:21
decisions.reason: Pharaoh's refusal does not take God by surprise.

decisions.choice: remained stubborn
decisions.reason: A heart that "is strong" against God is stubborn; Literal keeps "strong", as in 4:21.

decisions.choice: Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names the people "them" refers to.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה כָּבֵ֖ד לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה מֵאֵ֖ן לְשַׁלַּ֥ח הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, heavy [is the] heart of Pharaoh; he refuses to let go the people.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Pharaoh is stubborn at heart and will not release the people.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "The heart of Pharaoh [is] heavy; he refuses to let the people go.

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Pharaoh is very stubborn. He will not let the people go.

decisions.choice: heavy: dull, unmoved, unwilling to respond
decisions.reason: A "heavy" heart does not respond, as heavy ears do not hear (Isaiah 6:10) and heavy eyes do not see (Genesis 48:10). Pharaoh made the Israelites' labor "heavy" (5:9); now his own heart is heavy. See the note on 7:3.

decisions.choice: stubborn at heart (Balanced); very stubborn (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "heavy" so the three verbs for Pharaoh's heart stay distinct; Balanced and Readable say what a heavy heart is.

records.heading: The Nile turns to blood

records.source: לֵ֣ךְ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֞ה בַּבֹּ֗קֶר הִנֵּה֙ יֹצֵ֣א הַמַּ֔יְמָה וְנִצַּבְתָּ֥ לִקְרָאת֖וֹ עַל־שְׂפַ֣ת הַיְאֹ֑ר וְהַמַּטֶּ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ לְנָחָ֖שׁ תִּקַּ֥ח בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Go to Pharaoh in the morning; look, he [is] going out to the water, and you will station yourself to meet him on [the] bank of the River; and the staff which was turned into [a] snake you will take in your hand.
pieces: Go to Pharaoh in the morning, when he goes out to the water. Wait for him on the bank of the Nile, and have in your hand the staff that turned into a snake.

L.15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning; look, he [is] going out to the water. And you shall station yourself to meet him on the bank of the River, and the staff that was turned into a snake you shall take in your hand.

R.15: In the morning, go to Pharaoh when he goes down to the water. Stand on the bank of the Nile River and wait for him there. Take along the staff that turned into a snake.

decisions.choice: the River: the Nile
decisions.reason: Egypt's great river is called simply "the River". All Egypt's life and farming depended on it, and its yearly flood was honored as a divine gift. The first plague strikes there.

decisions.choice: the staff that was turned into a snake: the staff of 4:2-4
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in 4:3, not the "serpent" of verses 9-12. The reminder points to the sign God first gave Moses.

decisions.choice: station yourself: take your stand, be waiting
decisions.reason: The verb means to stand firmly in place, ready to meet someone.

decisions.choice: the Nile
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the river; Literal keeps "the River".

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָעִבְרִים֙ שְׁלָחַ֤נִי אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וְיַֽעַבְדֻ֖נִי בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְהִנֵּ֥ה לֹא־שָׁמַ֖עְתָּ עַד־כֹּֽה׃
records.gloss: And you will say to him, Yahweh, [the] God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, let go my people, that they may serve me in the wilderness; and look, you have not listened until now.
pieces: Say to him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to tell you, "Release {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so they can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the wilderness." So far, you have refused to listen.

L.16: And you shall say to him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, "Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, that they may serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the wilderness." But look, you have not listened until now.

R.16: Tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to you. He says, "Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go so they can worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the desert." But you still have not obeyed.

decisions.choice: serve me: worship and belong to God as his servants
decisions.reason: The verb means both to work for someone and to worship. Israel served Egypt with hard labor (1:13-14); God calls them to serve him instead.

decisions.choice: the God of the Hebrews: the name Moses was told to use before Pharaoh
decisions.reason: God gave Moses these words in 3:18, and Moses used them in 5:3.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable uses "worship", the sense of "serve" that fits a journey into the wilderness to sacrifice; Literal and Balanced keep "serve".

records.source: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּזֹ֣את תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַכֶּ֣ה׀בַּמַּטֶּ֣ה אֲשֶׁר־בְּיָדִ֗י עַל־הַמַּ֛יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּיְאֹ֖ר וְנֶהֶפְכ֥וּ לְדָֽם׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh, by this you will know that I [am] Yahweh: look, I am striking with the staff which [is] in my hand on the water which [is] in the River, and they will be changed into blood.
pieces: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: "Here is how you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: I am about to strike the Nile's water with this staff in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand, and it will become blood.

L.17: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "By this you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: look, I am striking with the staff that [is] in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand on the water that [is] in the River, and it will be turned into blood.

R.17: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says, "This is how you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Look! I will strike the water of the Nile with the staff in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} hand. The water will turn into blood.

decisions.choice: I am striking with the staff in my hand: God acts through his messenger
alternatives: Moses speaks of his own hand
decisions.reason: The words are God's ("thus says Yahweh"), yet the staff is held by Moses and Aaron (verses 15, 19-20). The speaker's "I" passes between God and the one who speaks and acts for him, as Moses was made "God to Pharaoh" (verse 1). Verse 25 says that Yahweh struck the River.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am Yahweh: the answer to Pharaoh's "I do not know Yahweh" (5:2)
decisions.reason: See verse 5.

decisions.choice: blood: the water became blood
decisions.reason: The text calls it blood and gives its effects: dead fish, stench, water no one can drink (verses 18, 21). It does not explain the means.

records.source: וְהַדָּגָ֧ה אֲשֶׁר־בַּיְאֹ֛ר תָּמ֖וּת וּבָאַ֣שׁ הַיְאֹ֑ר וְנִלְא֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מַ֖יִם מִן־הַיְאֹֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And the fish which [is] in the River will die, and will stink the River, and will be weary Egypt to drink water from the River.
pieces: Its fish will die, the Nile will smell foul, and the Egyptians will be unable to stomach its water."'"

L.18: And the fish that [are] in the River will die, and the River will stink, and [the] Egyptians will weary of drinking water from the River."'"

R.18: The fish in the river will die, and the river will smell awful. The Egyptians will find that they cannot drink from it."'"

decisions.choice: be weary of drinking: try in vain, find it impossible
decisions.reason: The verb means to be worn out or to give up. The Egyptians will struggle to drink the water and fail (verse 21, "they could not drink").

decisions.choice: stink: the verb of 5:21
decisions.reason: The Israelite foremen said Moses and Aaron had made them "stink" before Pharaoh (5:21). Now the River of Egypt stinks.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֱמֹ֣ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֡ן קַ֣ח מַטְּךָ֣ וּנְטֵֽה־יָדְךָ֩ עַל־מֵימֵ֨י מִצְרַ֜יִם עַֽל־נַהֲרֹתָ֣ם׀עַל־יְאֹרֵיהֶ֣ם וְעַל־אַגְמֵיהֶ֗ם וְעַ֛ל כָּל־מִקְוֵ֥ה מֵימֵיהֶ֖ם וְיִֽהְיוּ־דָ֑ם וְהָ֤יָה דָם֙ בְּכָל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּבָעֵצִ֖ים וּבָאֲבָנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, say to Aaron, take your staff and stretch out your hand over [the] waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their canals, and over their pools, and over every gathering of their water, that they may become blood; and there will be blood in all [the] land of Egypt, and in wood and in stone.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Take your staff and hold out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over its branches of the Nile, its canals, its marshes, and every place where its water is collected, so that they become blood.' Blood will be found all through the land of Egypt, even in vessels of wood and of stone."

L.19: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Take your staff and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their canals, and over their pools, and over every gathering of their water, that they may become blood.' And there will be blood in all the land of Egypt, both in [vessels of] wood and in [vessels of] stone."

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Tell Aaron to take his staff and hold out his hand over all the water in Egypt: the rivers, the canals, the ponds, and every place where water is stored. All of it will turn into blood. There will be blood everywhere in Egypt, even in the wooden and stone jars that people keep water in."

decisions.choice: rivers, canals, pools, gatherings of water: every kind of water in Egypt
decisions.reason: The first two words are used of the branches of the Nile and the channels dug from it; the third of marshes and standing pools; the last of any place where water collects, such as reservoirs. Together they mean all the water of the land.

decisions.choice: in wood and in stone: in containers of wood and stone
decisions.reason: The phrase most likely means water already drawn and stored in wooden and stone vessels, so that even stored water became blood. Others take it of water in trees and in stone basins. The same pair of words is used elsewhere of idols (Deuteronomy 4:28), but nothing here points to idols.

decisions.choice: vessels of wood and of stone (Balanced); wooden and stone jars that people keep water in (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "in wood and in stone" refers to, following the note on these words; Literal brackets "vessels of".

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵן֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאַהֲרֹ֜ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר׀צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּ֤רֶם בַּמַּטֶּה֙ וַיַּ֤ךְ אֶת־הַמַּ֨יִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּיְאֹ֔ר לְעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וּלְעֵינֵ֖י עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיֵּהָֽפְכ֛וּ כָּל־הַמַּ֥יִם אֲשֶׁר־בַּיְאֹ֖ר לְדָֽם׃
records.gloss: And did so Moses and Aaron just as had commanded Yahweh, and he raised the staff and struck the water which [was] in the River before [the] eyes of Pharaoh and before [the] eyes of his servants, and were changed all the water which [was] in the River into blood.
pieces: Moses and Aaron did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded. While Pharaoh and his officials watched, he lifted up the staff and struck the water of the Nile, and all the water in the river was turned into blood.

L.20: And Moses and Aaron did so, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded; and he raised the staff and struck the water that [was] in the River before the eyes of Pharaoh and before the eyes of his servants, and all the water that [was] in the River was turned into blood.

R.20: Moses and Aaron did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them. Aaron raised his staff and hit the water of the Nile. Pharaoh and his officials saw it happen. All the water in the river turned into blood.

decisions.choice: he raised the staff and struck: most likely Aaron
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular and do not name the one who acts. Verse 19 tells Aaron to stretch out his hand with the staff, so he is most likely meant. Verses 15 and 17 speak of the staff in Moses' hand.

decisions.choice: before the eyes of Pharaoh: in his sight
decisions.reason: The sign is done openly, so that Pharaoh and his court see it.

decisions.choice: Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who raised the staff, following verse 19.

records.source: וְהַדָּגָ֨ה אֲשֶׁר־בַּיְאֹ֥ר מֵ֨תָה֙ וַיִּבְאַ֣שׁ הַיְאֹ֔ר וְלֹא־יָכְל֣וּ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מַ֖יִם מִן־הַיְאֹ֑ר וַיְהִ֥י הַדָּ֖ם בְּכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And the fish which [was] in the River died, and stank the River, and not were able Egypt to drink water from the River; and was the blood in all [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: The Nile's fish died and the river began to reek; the Egyptians could not drink from it. Throughout the land of Egypt there was blood.

L.21: And the fish that [were] in the River died, and the River stank, and [the] Egyptians could not drink water from the River; and the blood was in all the land of Egypt.

R.21: All the fish in the river died. The river smelled awful, and the Egyptians could not drink from it. There was blood in every part of Egypt.

decisions.choice: the fish died, the River stank, they could not drink: each thing God said in verse 18 happened
decisions.reason: The account repeats God's words almost exactly to show that they came true.

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ־כֵ֛ן חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם בְּלָטֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֶּחֱזַ֤ק לֵב־פַּרְעֹה֙ וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֣ע אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And did thus [the] magicians of Egypt by their enchantments, and was strong [the] heart of Pharaoh, and not he listened to them, just as had spoken Yahweh.
pieces: But the magicians of Egypt did the same with their spells, and Pharaoh's heart stayed stubborn. He did not listen to them; it happened as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

L.22: And the magicians of Egypt did thus by their enchantments; and the heart of Pharaoh was strong, and he did not listen to them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken.

R.22: But the Egyptian magicians used their magic and did the same thing. And Pharaoh stayed stubborn. He would not listen to Moses and Aaron. This is just what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said would happen.

decisions.choice: did thus: the magicians also turned water into blood
decisions.reason: The text does not say where they found water; verse 24 says the Egyptians dug for it. The magicians could add to the plague but not take it away.

decisions.choice: was strong: the same words as verse 13
decisions.reason: See the notes on 7:3 and 7:13.

decisions.choice: Moses and Aaron
decisions.reason: Readable names the people "them" refers to, as in verse 13.

records.source: וַיִּ֣פֶן פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־בֵּית֑וֹ וְלֹא־שָׁ֥ת לִבּ֖וֹ גַּם־לָזֹֽאת׃
records.gloss: And turned Pharaoh and went into his house, and not he set his heart also to this.
pieces: Pharaoh turned his back and went into his palace, giving no thought even to this.

L.23: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not set his heart even to this.

R.23: Pharaoh turned around and went back into his palace. Even this did not make him pay attention.

decisions.choice: he did not set his heart to this: he paid no attention to it
decisions.reason: To "set the heart" to something is to take it seriously (9:21; 1 Samuel 4:20). "Even this" sets the plague beside the sign of verses 10-12.

decisions.choice: his house: his palace
decisions.reason: A king's "house" is his palace.

records.source: וַיַּחְפְּר֧וּ כָל־מִצְרַ֛יִם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הַיְאֹ֖ר מַ֣יִם לִשְׁתּ֑וֹת כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽכְלוּ֙ לִשְׁתֹּ֔ת מִמֵּימֵ֖י הַיְאֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And dug all Egypt around the River [for] water to drink, for not they were able to drink from [the] water of the River.
pieces: Unable to drink the water of the Nile, all the Egyptians dug around the river to find water fit to drink.

L.24: And all the Egyptians dug around the River [for] water to drink, for they could not drink of the water of the River.

R.24: The Egyptians could not drink the water from the Nile. So they all dug holes near the river to find water to drink.

decisions.choice: dug around the River: dug in the ground near its banks
decisions.reason: The Egyptians looked for water that had not come straight from the River. The text does not say whether they found it.

records.source: וַיִּמָּלֵ֖א שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים אַחֲרֵ֥י הַכּוֹת־יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־הַיְאֹֽר׃פ
records.gloss: And were completed seven days after struck Yahweh the River.
pieces: After {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck the Nile, seven full days passed.

L.25: And seven days were completed after {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck the River.

R.25: After {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck the Nile, a whole week went by.

decisions.choice: Yahweh struck the River: the act was God's
decisions.reason: Aaron raised the staff (verse 20), but the text says it was Yahweh who struck the River, as God said in verse 17.

decisions.choice: seven days were completed: a full week
decisions.reason: The plague lasted, or at least seven days passed before the next word to Pharaoh. The verb means to be filled up.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, go to Pharaoh, and you will say to him, thus says Yahweh, let go my people, that they may serve me.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: "Release {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, so they can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.26: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and say to him, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go, that they may serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

R.26: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says, "Let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people go so they can worship {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: verse numbering: Hebrew 7:26-29 is 8:1-4 in many Bibles
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text, followed here, ends chapter 7 four verses later than many Bibles do. So Hebrew 7:26-29 is numbered 8:1-4 there, and Hebrew 8:1-28 is 8:5-32. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: let my people go, that they may serve me: the demand of verse 16 again
decisions.reason: God repeats the demand before each new plague (7:16; 9:1, 13; 10:3).

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, Readable uses "worship" for "serve".

records.heading: A warning of frogs

records.source: וְאִם־מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לְשַׁלֵּ֑חַ הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י נֹגֵ֛ף אֶת־כָּל־גְּבוּלְךָ֖ בַּֽצְפַרְדְּעִֽים׃
records.gloss: And if refusing you [are] to let [them] go, look, I am striking all your territory with frogs.
pieces: If you refuse to let them go, watch: I will strike your whole country with frogs.

L.27: And if you refuse to let [them] go, look, I am striking all your territory with frogs.

R.27: If you refuse to let them go, I will strike your whole country with frogs.

decisions.choice: striking: bringing a blow or plague on
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a blow that brings harm or disease; the noun from it is "plague" (9:14; 12:13).

decisions.choice: frogs: from the River into the land
decisions.reason: Frogs bred in the Nile and its marshes; here they leave it and fill the land.

records.source: וְשָׁרַ֣ץ הַיְאֹר֮ צְפַרְדְּעִים֒ וְעָלוּ֙ וּבָ֣אוּ בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ וּבַחֲדַ֥ר מִשְׁכָּבְךָ֖ וְעַל־מִטָּתֶ֑ךָ וּבְבֵ֤ית עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ וּבְעַמֶּ֔ךָ וּבְתַנּוּרֶ֖יךָ וּבְמִשְׁאֲרוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And will swarm the River [with] frogs, and they will come up and come into your house and into [the] room of your bed and on your bed and into [the] house of your servants and on your people and into your ovens and into your kneading bowls.
pieces: The Nile will swarm with frogs. They will climb out and get into your palace, into the room where you sleep and onto your bed, into your officials' houses and onto your people, into your ovens and the bowls you knead dough in.

L.28: And the River will swarm [with] frogs, and they will come up and come into your house and into the room where you lie down and onto your bed, and into the house of your servants and onto your people, and into your ovens and into your kneading bowls.

R.28: The Nile will be full of frogs. They will come out of the river and go into your palace. They will get into your bedroom and onto your bed. They will go into your officials' houses and onto your people. They will even get into your ovens and the bowls where you mix bread dough.

decisions.choice: swarm: the verb of 1:7
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the waters teeming with creatures (Genesis 1:20-21) and of Israel multiplying in Egypt (1:7). Pharaoh tried to stop Israel's increase; now the River swarms against him.

decisions.choice: ovens and kneading bowls: where bread was made
decisions.reason: Dough was mixed in bowls and baked in clay ovens; the frogs reach even the family's food.

decisions.choice: the room of your lying down: your bedroom
decisions.reason: The phrase is the room where a person sleeps (2 Kings 6:12).

records.source: וּבְכָ֥ה וּֽבְעַמְּךָ֖ וּבְכָל־עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ יַעֲל֖וּ הַֽצְפַרְדְּעִֽים׃
records.gloss: And on you and on your people and on all your servants will come up the frogs.
pieces: On you, on your people, and on all your officials the frogs will climb."'"

L.29: And on you and on your people and on all your servants the frogs will come up."'"

R.29: The frogs will jump up onto you, onto your people, and onto all your officials."'"

decisions.choice: on you ... will come up: the list ends with Pharaoh himself
decisions.reason: The order puts Pharaoh, his people and his officials first, then the frogs. No one in Egypt, from the king down, escapes.
